facts.raw_span: Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region
Visual acuity: 20/25 to 20/30 in both eyes (OU)
Few yellow spots present, no pigmentary degeneration
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades
Large, slow scotopic and photopic responses
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in superotemporal region

concepts.why: Night blindness since childhood, flat rod electroretinogram, and complete loss of photoreceptors in the superotemporal region are characteristic of Retinitis pigmentosa
Yellow spots and hypofluorescence in the superotemporal zones are consistent with Choroidal dystrophy
Visual acuity of 20/25 to 20/30 and large, slow scotopic and photopic responses are suggestive of Cone-rod dystrophy
Night blindness since childhood and flat rod electroretinogram are characteristic of Leber congenital amaurosis
Inferonasal scotoma on Goldmann visual field is consistent with Optic neuropathy
Indistinct grayish circle beyond the arcades may be indicative of Pseudotumor cerebri
Night blindness since childhood with no other symptoms is consistent with Congenital stationary night blindness
Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region may be indicative of Retinal detachment

rationales.F01: Night blindness since childhood is a key symptom of retinitis pigmentosa, cone-rod dystrophy, and congenital stationary night blindness.
rationales.F07: Inferonasal scotoma is a characteristic visual field defect in retinitis pigmentosa and cone-rod dystrophy.
rationales.F09: Flat rod electroretinogram is a diagnostic feature of retinitis pigmentosa and congenital stationary night blindness.
rationales.F11: Complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region is consistent with advanced retinitis pigmentosa, cone-rod dystrophy, and choroidal dystrophy.
